authentication.credentialCreation: Sign in to the local UniFi application, open Integrations, select "Create New API Key"; the key is displayed once (developer.ui.com Getting Started, "Local" connection type).

notes: OpenAPI declares two servers: "UniFi API Cloud Connector" (api.ui.com, forbidden by design, spec §1.2) and "Local Console" https://{consoleIP}/proxy/network/integration. Adapters use only the local server.
OpenAPI declares no securitySchemes; the X-API-KEY header is specified in portal prose and the developer.ui.com llms.txt index.

The OpenAPI documents only 2xx responses. The Error Handling page documents the error body: statusCode, statusName, code (e.g. api.authentication.missing-credentials), message, timestamp, requestPath (e.g. /integration/v1/sites/123), requestId (UUID, for 500s).
Documented action enums: device action RESTART; port action POWER_CYCLE; client actions AUTHORIZE_GUEST_ACCESS and UNAUTHORIZE_GUEST_ACCESS.
Credential-bearing fields in schemas: Hotspot voucher `code`; Wi-Fi pre-shared key `passphrase`.
The developer portal publishes Network API documentation for versions 9.1.120 through 11.0.97; older consoles may expose fewer operations (spec §19).

Observed 2026-11-11 by the opt-in live read-only test (Network 11.0.99; not stated by the vendor): an API key created under Integrations in UniFi Network also authorises the Protect integration API on the same console. Protect accepted it and rejected a random key. Treat it as a console-wide administrative credential.

Observed 2026-11-11 (same run): a Site Manager key from unifi.ui.com is rejected locally with HTTP 401. Paging (offset and limit, across two pages) and a documented filter expression worked. The service passes filter expressions on unchanged; the console validates them.
Observed 2026-11-11 (Network 11.0.99; no vendor statement found): the Create API Key dialog asks only for a name, with no scope, application or read-only choice. Keys have full administrative scope.
unverified: Header casing differs between sources (X-API-KEY vs X-API-Key). HTTP header names are case-insensitive, so this is cosmetic.
Local API rate limits are not documented.
The vendor gives no TLS trust guidance for the local console certificate; per-console CA or pin is required by spec §4.4.
